$comment: THE OPENROUTER/MINIMAX PROVIDER SET. Set-SPECIFIC declarations only — which models, which ladders, which runner. Set-INDEPENDENT budgets (effortTiers, roleOverrides, outputTokenFloors) stay in llm-defaults.json and are shared by every set, so swapping providers never changes how much budget a tier gets.
$provenance: ladders, ladderTierOrder and modelOverrides were MOVED VERBATIM from projects/metrolinx/llm-settings.json on 2026-08-25 — generated from that file, not retyped. metrolinx is the live client codeline, so its chain is the one the openrouter stack keeps. mock3, hello-dolly and skyscanner previously topped out at glm-5.2/5.1 and now inherit glm-5.3: a deliberate convergence, recorded here rather than discovered later.

medium._why: M2.5 is legacy. M2.7 scores materially higher on multi-file and long-horizon work (NL2Repo 26.6 -> 39.8, MLE Bench Lite +15pts) and the -highspeed variant is documented as producing IDENTICAL results, only faster — so it is a free latency win, not a quality trade. The chain ends at glm-5.3 rather than 5.2 because 5.3's gains concentrate in agent-shaped tasks, which is what a seam that has already escalated twice is struggling with.

highest._why: glm-5.3 shares 5.2's base model; every gain is post-training on executable environments and long-horizon tasks — Terminal-Bench 3.0 4.6 -> 28.3, DeepSWE 46.2 -> 66.9, SWE-Marathon 19.4 -> 42.5. It also reaches a higher score with ~22% FEWER output tokens on hard work, which offsets most of the 45% higher per-token price. All vendor-reported: no independent reproduction exists yet.

minimax-m2.7._why: Replaces MiniMax-M2.5 as the medium tier's start. maxIterations is 90, not M2.5's 45: 45 was the outlier in this file (M3 120, glm 120, kimi-k3 150) and M2.7's advantage is precisely on the long-horizon work that needs room to converge — capping the stronger model at the weaker one's budget would throw the upgrade away. autoCompressAt is 150000 against a 204800 context: compaction destroys the cacheable prefix, so it must be an overflow guard near the ceiling, never a token-saving device. Substring is 'MiniMax-M2.7' so it matches the -highspeed variant too.

glm-5.3._why: Mirrors glm-5.2's sampling (same base model, so temperature/topP carry over) with more iteration room at 150, because this is now the highest tier's start and has only ONE rung above it. autoCompressAt raised to 300000 against a 1048576 context — 5.2's 180000 was conservative and every compaction destroys the cache. providerOrder is Z.AI because OpenRouter lists exactly one endpoint for this model; copying 5.2's CoreWeave pin would have failed every call.

modelOverrides.$miniTierWhy: miniTier marks the cheap, fast rung — the models that are quick but limited in generation capacity. It was decided in engine code by sniffing vendor naming habits (-mini, -flash, -haiku, minimax-m2), which breaks in both directions: a cheap model named differently read as capable, and a capable model containing -flash read as cheap. The set that declares the model declares its tier.

claude.$whyFlags: The same two knobs every stack exposes, so a seam's declared effort and compaction reach the runner here exactly as they do on the others. Naming them per set rather than in engine code is what makes a swap a config edit.
claude.$whyNoUnsetEnv: Deliberately empty. Scrubbing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY sends Claude Code to the OAuth credentials on disk and bills for real — recorded in seam-the-subscription-pays-not-the-api-key. This stack authenticates with OPENROUTER_API_KEY and has no reason to take anything away.

$whyRunners: THE SWAP MUST NOT INHERIT THE PREVIOUS STACK'S RUNNER. apply_runner_settings is called with the BASENAME of CLAUDE_CMD, which is 'claude' under every set, so a set declaring no runner by that name resolves nothing and the flags, env and scrubs of whatever ran before are simply carried over. claude, codemie and mockserver each declared one; this set did not, which made hot swap 2 the one stack that silently kept another stack's settings.
